overview: Pulmonary infiltration indicates the abnormal accumulation of cellular, liquid, or fibrotic substances within the lung parenchyma or interstitial spaces that are denser than normal aerated lung tissue.
radiographic_findings: Hazy, ill-defined opacity ('ground-glass' appearance or reticular interstitial markings)
Diffuse bilateral or perihilar reticulonodular interstitial patterns
Loss of crisp pulmonary vessel clarity without complete lobar consolidation
Preservation of underlying vascular margins through the hazy opacity
common_symptoms: Gradual onset or chronic exertional shortness of breath
Constitutional symptoms: low-grade fever, unintentional weight loss, night sweats
Velcro-like fine end-inspiratory crackles (crepitations) on pulmonary auscultation
causes_and_risk_factors: Infectious: Atypical bacterial pneumonia, viral pneumonitis (CMV, influenza, COVID-19), Pneumocystis jirovecii (PJP)
Non-infectious: Drug-induced pneumonitis (e.g., amiodarone, methotrexate, nitrofurantoin)
Autoimmune/Connective tissue diseases: Systemic sclerosis, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus
Occupational & environmental exposures: Asbestosis, silicosis, hypersensitivity pneumonitis
diagnostic_information: High-Resolution Computed Tomography (HRCT) of the Thorax (primary diagnostic tool for interstitial lung patterns)
Comprehensive Pulmonary Function Tests (PFTs) with DLCO (Diffusion Capacity for Carbon Monoxide)
Bronchoalveolar Lavage (BAL) and transbronchial biopsy if etiology remains uncertain
Serum autoimmune antibody panel (ANA, RF, Anti-CCP, Scl-70)
treatment_approaches: Prompt cessation and avoidance of causative inciting environmental antigens or medications
Antimicrobial therapy for documented opportunistic or atypical infections
Immunosuppressive regimens (corticosteroids, mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide) for inflammatory/autoimmune alveolitis
Antifibrotic pharmacotherapy (nintedanib, pirfenidone) in progressive fibrosing phenotypes
Ambulatory supplemental oxygen therapy as needed
when_to_seek_care: Rapid progression of breathlessness over days to weeks
Oxygen saturation falling below 90% at rest or with minimal exertion
New-onset fever in an immunocompromised host
